ety.text: Borrowed from Polish abecadło (“alphabet”) of 18th century, from Old Polish obiecadło adapted with suffix -dło. From Middle High German abecede. From the first four letters of the Latin alphabet. Compare Latin abecedārium. Cognate with Ukrainian абеца́дло (abecádlo).

s.g: to run for an election, to stand for election

ety.text: ве́ер (véjer) + -о- (-o-) + о́браз (óbraz) + -ный (-nyj), calque of Latin flabelliformis.

s.g: to smear on, to cover by smearing
to soil, to stain, to pollute
to use up by smearing on

ety.text: Borrowed from French journal (which also calqued into дневни́к (dnevník)). Further from Latin diurnālis, from diurnus, close akin to diurnum (whence French jour, whence дежу́рный (dežúrnyj)). Ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *dyew- (whence день (denʹ), ди́во (dívo)).

s.g: to obscure, to dim, to cloud, to fog
tool (mechanical device intended to make a task easier)

ety.text: Interpretation of Biblical Hebrew עֲזָאזֵל (“azazél”) (Leviticus 16:8, 10, 26); rendered as козёл для отпуще́ния (kozjól dlja otpuščénija) in Lev. 16:26 of the Russian Synodal Bible, and as козелъ, ѿпꙋщеный во ѿпꙋщенїе (kozelŭ, ōtŭpuštenyj vo ōtŭpuštenije) in the Elizabeth Bible.
From New Latin neurologia. By surface analysis, невро- (nevro-) + -логия (-logija). Also from French névrologie.

s.g: to overdo, to spoil by overdoing
to stand, to bear, to stomach

ety.text: Inherited from Old East Slavic печенѣгъ (pečeněgŭ), of Turkic origin and related to Turkish bacanak. Compare Hungarian besenyő.

ety.text: Directly from Romanian rumân, archaic form of român.

Inherited from Old East Slavic свинꙑ́и (svinýi), from Proto-Slavic *svinъ, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *swīˀnas, from Proto-Indo-European *suH-iHnos, from *suH- (“pig, hog, swine”) + *-iHnos. By surface analysis, сви(нья́) (svi(nʹjá)) + -но́й (-nój).
Inherited from Old East Slavic скуфиꙗ (skufija), from Ancient Greek σκούφια (skoúphia).
Inherited from Old East Slavic смьрдѣти (smĭrděti), from Proto-Slavic *smьrdě̀ti, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *smirˀdḗˀtei.

x: Разуми́хин, разуме́ется, был смешо́н с свое́ю внеза́пною, спья́ну загоре́вшеюся стра́стью к Авдо́тье Рома́новне; но, посмотре́в на Авдо́тью Рома́новну, осо́бенно тепе́рь, когда́ она́ ходи́ла, скрести́в ру́ки, по ко́мнате, гру́стная и заду́мчивая, мо́жет быть, мно́гие извини́ли бы его́, не говоря́ у…

ety.text: From теля́та (teljáta) + -ий (-ij), with irregular iotation (compare ребя́чий (rebjáčij) and щеня́чий (ščenjáčij)).
First attested in the 19th century. From Italian tor(so) + -е́ц (-éc).

x: Пьянчу́жка тако́й, потаску́н, тунея́дец служи́л пре́жде где́-то, да его́ за пья́ную жизнь уж давно́ из слу́жбы вы́ключили.

ety.text: Compound formed from Old Church Slavonic тоуне (tune) 'given freely; for no purpose' (also found in the adverb вту́не (vtúne)), and *я́дец (*jádec), 'eater' (related to еда́ (jedá, “food”)).
Borrowed from Estonian tups, with added -ик (-ik).
